# LastDB

> Massively multi-user apps with no central database.
>
> LastDB is one local daemon on each person's Mac (a node), reached over a Unix
> socket. Apps read and write it by key. A person can share a whole database
> with other people by invitation; the cloud in between carries end-to-end
> encrypted bytes and cannot read them. All app code runs on the users' machines.
> Starter apps install from the App Registry: Brain and LastSecrets. You can
> write your own app on the same socket and publish it to the registry.
>
> Local use needs no account. Optional cloud backup connects your local database
> with `lastdb backup connect`. Paid cloud storage is set up with `lastdb cloud`.

Website: https://thelastdb.com
Pages are prerendered at build time so agents and curl can read them without executing JavaScript.

Status: alpha. macOS on Apple Silicon only.

## Understand LastDB

Interactive system guide: https://thelastdb.com/explore/#diagram
Explore 146 parts across memory, disk, cloud, sharing, the data model, protection, data lifetime, and services.
Each part explains its purpose, connections, example, and limits.
It describes source from 27 November 2026, including tombstone-triggered sealing, private fault reporting, sharing approval, whole-record last-writer-wins, and the remaining delivery and restore limits.
JavaScript enables the diagram. Public design notes: https://thelastdb.com/explore/sources/design-notes.html

## Install (macOS Apple Silicon)

Needs Bun on PATH. The app installs run `bun install`.

Recommended: the installer script. Read it first: https://thelastdb.com/install.sh

```bash
curl -fsSL https://thelastdb.com/install.sh -o install.sh
sh install.sh
```

The first run downloads and checks the signed stable release, installs LastDB as a service that updates itself, prints the install plan for each starter app, and stops.
It ends with `RESULT: CONSENT NEEDED` (exit 3). That stop is expected. Read the plan. Then run:

```bash
sh install.sh --accept-install
brain init
```

The second run ends with `RESULT: PASS` when the apps are current and healthy.
`RESULT: FAIL` means a step failed; the line above it says which one. Running the script again is safe.
An agent must not pass `--accept-install` before the user has read the plan.

The same steps by hand. Paste-safe for macOS zsh: the block has no `#` comment lines.

```bash
brew install edgevector/lastdb/lastdb
lastdb service install
lastdb status
curl --fail --silent --show-error --unix-socket ~/.lastdb/data/folddb.sock http://localhost/health
lastdb app list
lastdb app install brain lastsecrets
```

The first `lastdb app install` prints the install plan for each app and stops.
Read the plan. Then run the same command again with `--accept-install`.

```bash
lastdb app install brain lastsecrets --accept-install
lastdb app status
brain init
```

The health check returns JSON with `"status":"ok"`. The socket path is `~/.lastdb/data/folddb.sock`.
Use `lastdb status` for host vitals and request activity.

On the first LastDB start, save any recovery phrase in a password manager.
Never put the phrase in chat, a source file, or a log.

## What the install changes

- The installer downloads the signed stable release, checks its sha256, and runs `lastdb service install`. That sets LastDB up as a login service and adds an hourly update check. LastDB then updates itself (see Upgrading LastDB).
- The App Registry clones each app into `~/.local/share/lastdb-apps/<app>/` and links its commands into `~/.local/bin`.
- Each app installs its own packages with Bun.
- On macOS, the first app install adds a LaunchAgent, `com.edgevector.lastdb-app-registry`. It checks the registry every 60 seconds and upgrades the installed apps on the stable channel.
- Nothing edits the shell profile. If `~/.local/bin` is not on PATH, add it yourself.
- Your data is in `~/.lastdb`.

## Remove it

Your data stays in `~/.lastdb`. These steps do not touch it.

```bash
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.edgevector.lastdb-app-registry"
rm "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/com.edgevector.lastdb-app-registry.plist"
rm -rf "$HOME/.local/share/lastdb-apps" "$HOME/.local/state/lastdb-app-registry"
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)/com.edgevector.lastdbd"
rm "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/com.edgevector.lastdbd.plist"
rm "$HOME/.local/bin/lastdb"
```

## Database only

```bash
brew install edgevector/lastdb/lastdb
lastdb service install
```

The package ships `lastdbd` (the daemon) and `lastdb` (the control CLI).
Run `lastdb --help` to see the commands for your installed release.

## Upgrading LastDB

Page: https://thelastdb.com/docs/upgrading

After `lastdb service install`, LastDB updates itself. Homebrew and the installer script are two ways to install; both end there.
`brew upgrade lastdb` only refreshes the installer copy kept by Homebrew. It does not replace the running service.

How it works: LastDB reads a release list signed by LastDB over HTTPS and checks the signature with a public key built into the binary.
It downloads the new `lastdb` and `lastdbd` into a staging folder, checks their hashes (and Apple signing and notarization on macOS),
and refuses a release whose home data format differs. It then stops taking writes, sends what it holds to the cloud backup if one is connected,
stops the daemon cleanly, moves the `~/.lastdb/current` link to the new pair, starts it, verifies it, and watches it for about five minutes.
If a check fails it returns to the previous pair on its own and will not try that version again by itself.

```bash
lastdb upgrade --check
lastdb upgrade
lastdb upgrade --status
lastdb upgrade --version <v>
lastdb upgrade --channel <stable|nightly>
lastdb upgrade --rollback
```

- `lastdb upgrade` installs the newest active release that is newer than the running one. By hand it ignores the staged rollout share.
- `--check` verifies the list and says what would install. `--status` prints the state. `--json` prints JSON.
- `--version <v>` installs one named active release. `--channel` switches the channel and installs its newest active release.
- `--rollback` returns to the previous pair and marks the left version rejected. `--clear-rejected <v>` removes the mark.
- `--accept-backup-behind` continues when the cloud backup is behind. The local data is intact; the accepted cost is an older cloud recovery point. Automatic runs never use it.
- `--pair <dir>` installs a pair you supply. It has no list entry, so it is never replaced automatically.
- Exit codes: 0 upgraded or already current, 2 refused before any change, 3 rolled back, 4 needs a person, 5 busy.

Automatic upgrades are set in `~/.lastdb/upgrade/config.toml`:

```toml
channel = "stable"
auto = "apply"
window = "02:00-05:00"
```

- `auto`: `apply` checks hourly and installs inside the window; `check` records what is available and never installs; `off` does neither.
- `channel`: `stable` (qualified releases, staged rollout) or `nightly` (daily build, no staged rollout).
- `window`: the local-time hours when an automatic install may run.
- The hourly check is part of the app-registry LaunchAgent (`com.edgevector.lastdb-app-registry`).

Staged rollout: a new stable release starts at 10 percent of installs, moves to 50 percent after 24 hours and 100 percent after 48 hours.
Each install decides its share locally from a random install id that is never sent anywhere. A hand-run upgrade does not wait for the share.

Rollback and withdrawal: the previous pair stays on disk, so going back needs no network. A release the project withdraws is marked in the signed list and is never offered again;
a fix is a new version. A running withdrawn release is rolled back at the next hourly check when `auto` is `apply`, even outside the window.

## App Registry

The App Registry is the install path for apps. It is a signed list. No account is needed.

`lastdb app list` shows the apps proved with your LastDB release. Install checks out the
exact proved commit, not `main`. Each app is proved in a fresh home before it is listed.
If no entry is proved with your release, install stops. Upgrade LastDB with
`lastdb upgrade`, or wait for the next proved set.

```bash
lastdb app list
lastdb app install brain
lastdb app upgrade brain
lastdb app status
```

- `lastdb app install <app>` installs one or more apps at their proved commit.
- `lastdb app upgrade <app>` moves an app to the newest proved commit. Use `--all` for every app.
- `lastdb app status` shows what is installed and the active release. Add `--check` to run the app's own checks.
- `lastdb app rollback <app>` returns an app to its previous release.

The list changes as apps are proved. Trust `lastdb app list` on the machine over any list on a web page.

## Apps: first commands

Brain (long-term notes and decisions):

```bash
brain init
brain concept new hello --title "Hello" --body "my first note"
brain get hello
brain ask "first note"
```

`brain get` reads by name. `brain ask` matches by keyword until LastSeek is installed; use a term from the body.
`brain mcp` runs Brain as a stdio MCP server for an agent.

LastSecrets (credentials):

```bash
lastsecrets init
printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | lastsecrets put my-api-token \
  --label "My API token" \
  --provider example \
  --purpose demo \
  --env dev \
  --value-stdin
lastsecrets ref my-api-token
lastsecrets list
```

`lastsecrets ref` prints a `lastsecrets://…` locator. List and search always print `value=<redacted>`.

LastSeek (semantic search, coming): LastSeek keeps a semantic index beside the node. It is not in the App Registry yet. Until it is, Brain finds notes by name and by keyword.
Do not install the older Search app on a new machine.

## Secrets policy (agents)

- Store with `lastsecrets put <slug> … --value-stdin` (value on stdin only).
- Persist only `lastsecrets://<slug>` locators in Brain, docs, CI, and logs.
- Retrieve with `lastsecrets get <slug>` only at the point of use; do not print or re-store the value.
- If LastSecrets is unavailable, stop before handling raw secret material.

## Mental model

- **LastDB**: the database. Login service `com.edgevector.lastdbd` (set up by `lastdb service install`), daemon `lastdbd`.
- **Schemas and keys**: a schema names its fields, its primary key, and any named alternate keys.
  A query needs a key (a hash, or a hash plus a range). A read with no key is refused.
  `lastdb get-keys` lists the keys of one schema, one page at a time. It does not return field values.
- **Apps**: programs that talk to the node over the socket (`brain`, `lastsecrets`, and your own).
- **LastSeek**: a semantic index beside the node. It is not part of the database, and it is not in the App Registry yet.
- **App Registry**: the signed list of apps you install by name with `lastdb app install`.

Socket: `~/.lastdb/data/folddb.sock` (Unix socket). The file name is historical; the product is LastDB.

## Build your own app

The developer guide has working requests for each step: declare a schema, write a record,
read it by primary key, read it by alternate key, and list keys.
https://thelastdb.com/developer

## Share a database

A node holds several named databases. One person, the publisher, shares a whole
database with other people. Data for a different audience goes in a different database.

The recipient exports a contact file and sends it to the publisher:

```bash
lastdb share contact --out ben.contact
```

The publisher creates a database and writes an invitation that only that recipient can open.
Each side gets the other's public key over a channel they already trust.

```bash
lastdb db create family-notes
lastdb --db family-notes share invite --recipient ben.contact --recipient-key "$BEN_KEY" --out ben.invite
```

The recipient accepts. The database then appears on their node and stays in step.

```bash
lastdb share accept --publisher "$ANA_KEY" --name family-notes ben.invite
```

Everyone invited can read the database. The publisher grants writing with
`lastdb share contributors grant` and removes it with `lastdb share contributors revoke`.
A change from another person goes, encrypted, to the publisher's node. That node checks it
against the sharing rules and the schema before anyone else receives it.
The cloud is a central service that stores and passes along encrypted bytes. It is not peer-to-peer.

## Publish an app

An app has no server. A release is a signed entry in the App Registry.

```bash
lastdb app publish --manifest manifest.json
```

Each person installs the app by name with `lastdb app install <app>`.
Publishing needs a paid Exemem subscription; Exemem is the cloud service LastDB uses for backup and sharing.
People who use a published app pay nothing to use it. Building and running an app locally needs no subscription.
